slides.title: Question 1: Pure Functions
slides.prompt: Which of the following describes a Pure Function?
options: Produces same output for same input with no side effects
slides.correctAnswer: Produces same output for same input with no side effects

slides.prompt: Fill in the function from `operator` module equivalent to `lambda x, y: x + y`.

slides.title: Question 9: First-Class Functions
slides.prompt: What does 'first-class functions' mean in Python?
options: Functions can be passed as arguments, returned, and assigned to variables
Functions are executed before main script
slides.correctAnswer: Functions can be passed as arguments, returned, and assigned to variables

slides.title: Question 10: List Comprehension Filter
slides.prompt: Fill in the keyword to convert `filter(lambda x: x > 0, nums)` into comprehension.

slides.title: Question 11: Higher-Order Function Definition
options: A function that takes another function as argument or returns a function
A function with more than 5 arguments
A function declared inside a class
slides.correctAnswer: A function that takes another function as argument or returns a function

slides.title: Question 15: Map vs Starmap
slides.prompt: What is the key difference between `itertools.starmap` and `map`?
options: starmap unpacks tuple arguments from single iterable automatically
starmap returns a list instead of iterator
